# Badge

Group: Feedback. Import: `import { Badge } from 'lynn-ui';`

A Lynn pill badge.
 `<Badge>Beta</Badge>` alone is a complete blue-tinted pill.

## Usage

Reach for `status` when the label is one of the thirteen real site states (roadmap phases, score grades, lifecycle pills) and `tone` for anything else. `bordered` adds the 20%-accent outline the Figma / Chrome / both target badges use. The system convention for a Superpowers/MCP-only feature is `tone="lynn"` with `icon={<IconBolt />}`.

## Don't

Don't pass `status` and `tone` together - `status` wins and both `tone` and `bordered` are dropped on the floor, so the badge you get is not the one you wrote. And don't invent a status by passing an accent that "looks right": the thirteen pairs are hand-tuned and are what the legends elsewhere on a page are explaining.

## Props

- `children: ReactNode` - Badge label.
- `tone?: AccentColor` - Tinted pill in one of Lynn's seven accents, at 14% background opacity. Ignored when `status` is set.
- `status?: BadgeStatus` - One of the status pills. These carry their own hand-tuned background/foreground pairs (e.g. `active` is a lightened `#6ab4ff` on 20% blue, not the flat `tone="blue"` pair), so a status badge deliberately overrides `tone`.
- `bordered?: boolean` - Adds the 20%-opacity accent border used by the Figma / Chrome / both target-badge family on tools.html. Those badges are otherwise identical to `tone="blue" | "emerald" | "teal"`, which is why they need no separate variant.
- `icon?: ReactNode` - Leading glyph. The system convention is a `lynn`-tinted bolt icon on every Superpowers/MCP-only feature: `<Badge tone="lynn" icon={<IconBolt />}>`.
- `className?: string`
- `style?: CSSProperties`
